name: RTX 3070 tech tree
scope: Get the most real work from one RTX 3070 8 GB (LHR included) for local LLMs and agent work.

status_values.measured: Done. result holds measured values with source paths.
status_values.paused: Started, then stopped. Not measured, so dependents wait. It restarts from scratch on the next run.
status_values.queued: Ready, or ready once its prereqs are measured.
status_values.needs_owner: Needs the owner present or the owner's go. The runner skips it.
status_values.blocked: A prereq is needs_owner or blocked. The runner skips it.

rules: Run a node only when every prereq has status measured.
Pick the first runnable node in next_order.
Each result entry has metric, value, source (a path relative to the repo root) and an optional note.
Label every number with n, warm or cold, and its confounds. Never invent a number.

limits: Do not change the power limit, clocks or undervolt.
Do not reboot, shut down or sleep the machine while unlocked.
Do not write firmware, VBIOS, ESP, BCD or NVRAM.
A WSL2 memory-cap change needs the owner's go.
Cold-boot arms need the owner present.
Stop if the screen blanks under load and log power and temperature.

measurement_rules: State n for every number. llama-bench uses -r 5 and 3 reps where possible.
Label warm or cold. All results in v1.3.0 are warm.
Keep the display on the integrated GPU for A/B runs, or label the confound.
Report pass rates with 95% confidence intervals.
A target is a goal, not a result.

baseline.label: unlocked agent bench, partial offload, warm
baseline.inferred_note: The -ngl, ctx and KV values are the lab defaults at that time. They are inferred from the serve script defaults, not from a log of the launch line.

tiers.title: Foundation
tiers.goal: Know the stack, measure it the same way every time, and confirm the FP32-accumulate unlock.

tiers.title: Inference
tiers.goal: Get the most tokens per second from 8 GB of VRAM.

tiers.title: Agent reliability
tiers.goal: Make more agent tasks pass on the same model and card.

tiers.title: Throughput
tiers.goal: Keep the card busy while agents wait on builds and tests.

tiers.title: Efficiency
tiers.goal: Measure energy per passing task. Do not tune power.

tiers.title: Capstones
tiers.goal: Combine the wins into a bigger model class and more useful work per Wh.

nodes.metric: Recorded fields present in each session meta file (yes/no).

nodes.title: Measurement harness
nodes.goal: Run the same benchmarks the same way, with n, variance and warm or cold state labeled on every number.
nodes.test: llama-bench with -r 5 and 3 reps for raw speed. A 12-task agent coding bench (6 roles x 2 tasks, hidden checks) at n=3 per task (36 runs). Board power sampled every 5 s. Summaries with 95% confidence intervals.
nodes.metric: Pass rate with 95% CI, passes per hour, median output tok/s, board Wh per task, run-to-run spread.
nodes.target: Target: every result states n, warm or cold, and its confounds.

result.metric: agent bench passes per hour (unlocked, serial)

confounds: All runs so far are warm. The cold-start fields are null.
The agent is not deterministic. n=3 per task is small.
The locked arm has n=2 per task and the unlocked arm has n=3 per task.
safety_notes: The harness only reads GPU state.

nodes.title: FP32-accumulate unlock
nodes.goal: Confirm that FP16 tensor-core math with FP32 accumulate runs at the full rate.
nodes.test: MMA microbenchmark: FP16 inputs with FP32 accumulate vs FP16 accumulate. Then a GEMM diagnostic at model-shaped sizes.
nodes.metric: mma ratio = FP32-acc rate / FP16-acc rate. Locked GeForce Ampere is near 0.5. Unlocked is near 1.0.
nodes.target: Target: ratio 1.0 in every unlocked session.
confounds: No locked GEMM baseline exists.
The mma test is a per-warp synthetic test, not dense GEMM.
safety_notes: No firmware, ESP, BCD or NVRAM writes from the lab.
No reboot or sleep while unlocked.

nodes.test: Read-only: free -g and nproc inside WSL2. Read the context percentiles from existing agent runs.
nodes.metric: Total RAM, WSL2 memory limit, free RAM with the lab server loaded, p95 of per-run max context.
nodes.target: Target: values recorded. The MoE node needs this result before the owner decides on the memory cap.

nodes.title: Cold-boot arms
nodes.goal: Measure power-on to first token and power-on to first passing task, for unlocked and locked boots.
nodes.test: The owner cold-boots the machine and marks power-on and unlock-done times. The harness records boot, WSL up, server start, model ready, first token, warm, first pass.
nodes.metric: Time to first token (s), time to first passing task (s), per arm.
nodes.target: Target: both arms measured with n of at least 3 boots each.
confounds: Display GPU must be the same in both arms.
safety_notes: Cold-boot arms need the owner present.
No unattended unlock boots.

nodes.title: Clean locked vs unlocked A/B
nodes.goal: Remove the display confound from the unlock comparison.
nodes.test: A locked cold boot with the display on the integrated GPU. Run the same llama-bench, GEMM, fa-off and agent bench as the unlocked arm.
nodes.metric: Delta per metric, locked vs unlocked, same display state.
nodes.target: Target: every unlock claim has a same-display locked baseline.
confounds: Today the locked runs had the display on the RTX card (about 850 MiB more VRAM in use).
safety_notes: A locked arm needs a cold boot without the unlock, with the owner present.

nodes.title: Fit map for an 8 GB card
nodes.goal: Find which model, quant, context and KV cache settings fit fully on an 8 GB card, and how fast each runs.
nodes.test: Qwen3-8B at Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, Q6_K and Q8_0, Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M, a 4B-class and a 14B-class Q4_K_M, all layers on the GPU, FA on. For each KV pair (f16, q8_0, q4_0), find the largest ctx that loads and serves a 512-token prompt. Record peak VRAM and llama-bench pp512/tg128 (n=3).
nodes.metric: Max ctx, VRAM MiB, pp512 and tg128 tok/s.
nodes.target: Target: a table of every model, quant and KV pair with its max ctx, peak VRAM and speed.
confounds: The display must be off the card, or the free VRAM is lower. Label it.
safety_notes: No power or clock changes.

nodes.title: Partial offload speed curve
nodes.goal: Show how speed falls as layers move from the card to system RAM.
nodes.test: llama-bench pp512/tg128 for Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M at -ngl 0, 8, 16, 24, 30 and all layers, ctx 4096, n=3. Then a 14B-class model up to the most layers that fit. Log VRAM and board power.
nodes.metric: pp512 and tg128 tok/s per -ngl, VRAM MiB, board W.
nodes.target: Target: a speed curve per model from -ngl 0 to all layers.
confounds: System RAM speed and CPU threads set the slow end of the curve.
safety_notes: No power or clock changes.

nodes.title: Weight quant choice
nodes.goal: Find the weight quant with the best passes per hour that fits at full offload.
nodes.test: Same model at Q4_K_M, IQ4_XS and Q5_K_M (if it fits). llama-bench, then the 36-run agent bench at the full-offload settings.
nodes.metric: Pass rate, passes per hour, decode tok/s, VRAM headroom.
nodes.target: Target: pick the quant with the most passes per hour. No out-of-memory errors.
confounds: A larger quant cuts the room for KV cache and parallel slots.

nodes.title: Speculative decoding: n-gram
nodes.goal: Speed up decode on edit-heavy roles with no extra VRAM.
nodes.test: Turn on the n-gram lookup mode of your llama.cpp build (check llama-server --help). Run the token bench and the 36-run agent bench.
nodes.metric: Agent decode tok/s, draft acceptance rate, pass rate, Wh per pass.
nodes.target: Target: agent decode at least 1.3x with the same pass rate.
confounds: Gains drop when the model thinks before it writes code (Fronde report).

nodes.title: Speculative decoding: draft model
nodes.goal: Speed up code and JSON output with a small draft model.
nodes.test: llama-server -md Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf with a draft length of 8-12, if VRAM allows at full offload.
nodes.metric: Agent decode tok/s, acceptance rate, VRAM, pass rate.
nodes.target: Target: agent decode at least 1.3x over n-gram mode or over no speculation.
confounds: The draft model takes VRAM from the KV cache.

nodes.title: Newer small dense model at full offload
nodes.goal: Test whether a newer small model (Qwen3.5-9B) passes more tasks at a similar speed.
nodes.test: Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M at -ngl 99. Check the chat and tool-call template. llama-bench pp512/pp4096/tg128, then the 36-run agent bench.
nodes.metric: Pass rate, decode tok/s, prefill tok/s.
nodes.target: Target: at least 10 of 36 passes at 40 tok/s or more.
confounds: Its hybrid layers may lack a fast CUDA prefill path in this build (llama.cpp issue #22967).

nodes.title: MoE expert offload (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B)
nodes.goal: Run a 35B-total, 3B-active MoE model with some experts in system RAM.
nodes.test: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-IQ4_XS (unsloth GGUF, 17.7 GB), same llama.cpp build. 1) llama-bench sweep at --n-cpu-moe 24, 27 and 30 (pp512, pp4096, tg128), with RAM, swap and VRAM logged. 2) Server fit ladder: ctx 16384 with KV q8_0, then KV q4_0, then ctx 12288, then ctx 8192. Each step must pass health, a 6000-token request and the VRAM and RAM limits. 3) 36-run core agent bench on the best fitting step. 4) Restore the Qwen3-8B best config and verify it, also on failure.
nodes.metric: llama-bench pp512, pp4096 and tg128 per n-cpu-moe, with RAM and VRAM peaks. Agent bench: passes per hour, pass rate, median output tok/s, board Wh per task and per pass, RAM available minimum, swap use, truncations per role.
nodes.target: Target: at least 10 of 36 passes and agent decode at least 18 tok/s. A win does not replace the best config, because the model changes.
confounds: CPU-side experts compete with build and test jobs for the CPU.
Public speed reports come from other machines with different RAM.
The thinking-off template path and the 8B sampler defaults (temp 0.2, top-p 0.95, top-k 20) are kept. The model card suggests other sampler values (GGUF default temp 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20).
The model is served under two aliases, its own name and the 8B id that pi sends, so pi and the harness need no change. Logs show the 8B id in requests.
The download ran during the tool-call-format and loop-guard benches, throttled (about 30 MB/s, idle IO class, lowest CPU priority). Its time window is logged with the node.
At 16384 context the KV cache is small (10 full-attention layers with 2 KV heads), so context is unlikely to limit the fit. Expert RAM is the tight resource under the 23 GiB WSL2 cap.
No slot restore: the prompt cache starts cold.
System RAM risk: expert weights in RAM can push the 23 GiB WSL2 VM into swap.
safety_notes: Runs at the 24 GB WSL2 memory cap. A WSL2 restart stops lab services.
Do not reboot Windows for a WSL2 change.
Check the mma ratio after any WSL2 restart.
Only the lab server is stopped and restarted; never WSL2. No WSL2 or .wslconfig change.
The node halts the chain if the 8B restore cannot be verified.
nodes.public_note: The WSL2 memory cap is now 24 GB (WSL2 reports 23 GiB).

model_file.gguf: arch qwen35moe, 40 blocks (full attention every 4th, the rest linear attention), 256 experts, 8 active, 2 KV heads of 256, file_type 30 (IQ4_XS)
model_file.why: The requested quant exists under that exact name in the unsloth repo. The official Qwen GGUF repo is not public under that name.

nodes.title: Workloads that use the unlocked math
nodes.goal: Find end-to-end jobs that gain from FP32-accumulate FP16/BF16 math.
nodes.test: Unlocked arm: PyTorch fp16/bf16 matmul TFLOPS, an image-generation it/s run, and a BF16 vs F16 small-model llama-bench pp512/pp2048.
nodes.metric: End-to-end speed per workload. Later: ratio vs the clean locked arm.
nodes.target: Target: at least 1.4x on one end-to-end FP16/BF16 workload vs the locked arm.
confounds: The ratio needs the locked-ab node. Until then, report unlocked numbers only.
The 4-bit chat model barely uses this math path.
safety_notes: No power or clock changes.

nodes.title: Test-gated done
nodes.goal: Do not accept 'done' until format, vet, build and visible tests pass.
nodes.test: Before the agent can finish, run gofmt -l, go vet, go build and visible tests. On failure, return the output to the agent. 36-run agent bench.
nodes.metric: Pass rate, passes per hour, gofmt/build/vet failure count, false 'done' count.
nodes.target: Target: gofmt, build and vet failures cut by half or more. Passes per hour above full-offload (14.54).

result.value: Measured negative result. Reverted. 6 of 36 passes (same as full-offload), 9.64 passes per hour vs 14.54, 3.59 board Wh per task vs 2.33. gofmt, build and vet failures went from 16 to 15 of 30, so the gate did not cut them by half. It did not beat full-offload on passes per hour, so it is not carried into later nodes. The best config stays full-offload (base variant).
36-run core agent bench (n=3) of variant testgate (attempts 2) at the full-offload config, card headless.

nodes.title: Edit-tool reliability
nodes.goal: Cut edit-tool errors: oldText not found, not unique, or no change.
nodes.test: Edit-tool arm: precise mismatch errors (nearest match with line numbers, or the duplicate count), line-anchored edits, and a fuzzy match only on a unique hit after whitespace normalization. 36-run core agent bench on the current best config (variant editrel-on-base, or editrel-on-testgate if test-gate becomes best). The arm is opt-in in a separate patched pi copy; the live pi and the harness binary are unchanged.
nodes.metric: Edit-error rate per edit call (edit errors excluding output-limit truncations, over all edit calls), passes per hour and pass rate (n=36, core set) against the current best config. Secondary only: bash non-zero exits per bash call.
nodes.target: Target: edit-error rate per edit call cut by half (baseline 52 of 110 edit calls, 47.3%; 52 of 363 of all tool calls). Passes per hour not below the current best config.

result.value: Measured negative result. Reverted. 3 of 36 passes, 3.56 passes per hour vs 14.54, edit-error rate per edit call 0.67 vs 0.47, 4.90 board Wh per task vs 2.33. The best config stays full-offload (base variant).

Many bash non-zero exits are normal build or test failures that the agent must see.

The arm only applies a whitespace-normalized match when it is line-aligned and unique. pi's own fuzzy match also matched inside a line; that partial-line case now gets a nearest-match error instead. This is part of the arm.
The read tool shows no line numbers, so line anchors come from error messages, grep -n or read offsets. Read is left unchanged so that only the edit tool varies.
The 4 edit calls cut by the output limit count as edit calls but not as edit errors.

nodes.title: Sampler settings
nodes.goal: Use Qwen3's recommended non-thinking sampler instead of the lab defaults, and test presence penalty.
nodes.test: Two arms, 36-run core agent bench each, on the best config at launch (both arms share one base). sampler-a: Qwen3 non-thinking set (temperature 0.7, top-p 0.8, top-k 20), except that min-p stays at the server default 0.05; presence penalty 0. sampler-b: the same set with presence penalty 1.5. Label both 'Qwen3 set, except min-p'. Baseline: full-offload defaults, temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, min-p 0.05, presence penalty 0. The params are sent per request through a bench-only proxy. No server change. A preflight request checks the server's slot params before the bench starts.
nodes.metric: Passes per hour (decision), pass rate, loop events per run, tool-call errors, Wh per task, truncations per role.
nodes.target: Keep an arm only if its passes per hour beat the base config. If both do, keep the higher one. Loop events and pass rate are reported, not used to decide.
confounds: The thinking-mode set (temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, min-p 0) does not apply here, because thinking is off for every role in both arms. The earlier test text used it with presence 1.5.
The arms run one after the other, not interleaved. Each is compared with the same base run.
Min-p stays at the server default 0.05. Qwen3's own set uses min-p 0, so the arms are 'Qwen3 set, except min-p'.

nodes.title: Planner-only thinking
nodes.goal: Test whether thinking helps the planner role: thinking on for pm only, with a bounded reasoning budget.
nodes.test: Thinking on for the pm role only: enable_thinking with a 1024-token thinking budget per request, through a bench-only proxy. Every other role stays thinking-off. The server stays thinking-off by default, with no server change. A preflight checks the per-request override before the bench and stops the node if it fails. 36-run core agent bench on the best config.
nodes.metric: Passes per hour, pass rate (overall and pm), board Wh per task, truncated tool calls and length stops per role (baseline 9 of 363 calls in the full-offload run: write 5, edit 4).
nodes.target: Keep only if passes per hour beat the base config. Report the pm pass rate and pm truncations separately.

result.metric: baseline output-limit truncations, full-offload run (not this node's result)
result.value: 9 of 363 tool calls (write 5, edit 4). The earlier count of 14 included 5 bash errors by a keyword match.

confounds: Thinking tokens share pm's 4096-token output cap. pm truncations are logged, not capped.
If the server cannot switch thinking per request, the preflight stops the node before the bench. It does not fall back to a server-wide change.
pm keeps the base sampler. The thinking-mode sampler set is not applied, so only thinking changes.

nodes.title: Loop guard
nodes.goal: Stop the agent from repeating the same tool call.
nodes.test: After 3 identical tool calls, reset the turn with a short note to the agent. 36-run agent bench.
nodes.metric: Loop events per run, pass rate, wall time.
nodes.target: Target: loop events cut by half.

nodes.title: Stacked agent fixes on a held-out set
nodes.goal: Combine the fixes that helped and check them on tasks that were not used to tune them.
nodes.test: Turn on all fixes that won. Run the 36-run bench and a held-out task set.
nodes.metric: Pass rate on the tuned set and on the held-out set, reported apart.
nodes.target: Target: at least 10 of 36 passes (one-sided Fisher p about 0.03 vs 3 of 36).
confounds: Tuning on 12 tasks can overfit them.

nodes.title: Parallel slots
nodes.goal: Serve 2-4 requests at once to fill idle GPU time.
nodes.test: llama-server --parallel 1, 2, 4 with total context = slots x per-slot context. Token bench at each setting.
nodes.metric: Aggregate tok/s, per-request tok/s, aggregate tok/s per board W.
nodes.target: Target: aggregate tok/s per board W at least 1.5x at 4 slots.
confounds: Half-full batches can be the worst case (public reports).
safety_notes: Log power and temperature. Stop on any screen blanking.

nodes.title: Concurrent agent workers
nodes.goal: Run 2 agent jobs side by side.
nodes.test: Agent bench with 2 workers against a 2-slot server.
nodes.metric: Passes per hour, pass rate, CPU load.
nodes.target: Target: passes per hour at least 1.5x vs 1 worker.
confounds: Builds and tests compete for the CPU.
safety_notes: Stop on any screen blanking.

nodes.title: Best-of-N with a visible-test selector
nodes.goal: Turn spare capacity into more passes.
nodes.test: Best-of-3 on implementer and debugger roles. Pick the attempt whose build, vet and visible tests pass. Never use the hidden check.
nodes.metric: Role pass rate, passes per hour, Wh per pass.
nodes.target: Target: implementer + debugger from 0 of 12 to at least 3 of 12.

nodes.title: Board power logging
nodes.goal: Log board power for every task with full coverage.
nodes.test: nvidia-smi power.draw at 5 s, read-only, started before the first task.
nodes.metric: Board Wh per task, coverage share of tasks with power data.
nodes.target: Target: 100% of tasks covered.

result.metric: board Wh per task, locked / unlocked
board W mean during agent bench, locked
board peak W under llama load (pause bench)

confounds: Unlocked power data starts after the first tasks. Unlocked Wh per pass is null.
Board power only. The rest of the PC is not measured.
safety_notes: Read-only power queries. No power-limit changes.

nodes.title: Wh per passing task
nodes.goal: Report energy per passing task for every config.
nodes.test: Every agent bench reports board Wh per pass and tok/s per W. Add wall-meter data if a plug meter is fitted.
nodes.metric: Board Wh per pass (and wall Wh per pass when available).
nodes.target: Target: Wh per pass at least 30% lower than the locked baseline after full offload.
confounds: Few passes make Wh per pass noisy. Report the CI of the pass count.
safety_notes: Power-limit, clock and undervolt changes are off-limits.

nodes.title: Bigger model class on 8 GB
nodes.goal: Run a 35B-class model on 8 GB that beats the 8B baseline on passes per hour.
nodes.test: Best MoE settings plus the stacked agent fixes. 36-run bench and held-out set.
nodes.metric: Pass rate, passes per hour, Wh per pass vs the 8B stack.
nodes.target: Target: more passes per hour than the best 8B stack.
safety_notes: Waits on moe-offload.

nodes.title: Self-funding throughput: useful work per Wh
nodes.goal: Find the config with the most passing tasks per Wh and per hour on one card.
nodes.test: Combine the best inference, agent and throughput settings. Run a long agent bench with full power logs.
nodes.metric: Passing tasks per Wh, passing tasks per hour.
nodes.target: Target: passing tasks per Wh at least 2x the locked baseline.
safety_notes: No power changes.
